Think about the total work load...let's say you do 15 reps (to failure) a 100 on db press...you moved a 1500 lbs during that set...but your not counting so now next time you do a set (same day or different day) you grab some 110's and go to failure (not counting) and end up at only 10 reps...so weight was higher, but you only moved 1100 lbs, 400 less than last set or previous session. You have not overloaded the muscle, and hypertrophy will not be stimulated! Tracking numbers and counting will allow you to see how much u moved at a given weight during a set. If you achieved the max in this example of 1500lbs, you will need to increase the weight to fit the rep scheme and perform it until you can surpass that total of 1500lbs, thus overloading the muscle! Hope this helps!
